rubrics.justification: No image was available, and the response did not perform actual morphology assessment; it inferred embryo quality from cycle metrics rather than describing visible blastocyst features.
It thoroughly integrated age, diagnosis, ovarian reserve, oocyte maturity, endometrium, sperm parameters, BMI, and first-cycle status into prognosis and transfer planning.

The reasoning is structured and mostly logical, with appropriate acknowledgment of missing morphology, though some prognostic inferences from oocyte maturity and presumed blastocyst quality are somewhat speculative.

Recommendations are largely consistent with standard IVF practice, including SET in a good-prognosis young patient and avoiding unnecessary add-ons, though ERA/PGT-A discussion is somewhat broader than strictly guideline-driven.
Provides clear practical recommendations for current transfer management and contingency planning, though some suggestions remain general because embryo morphology and lab outcomes were unavailable.
